body: The Victorian Liberal Party has withdrawn its endorsement of Paul Lindemann, its candidate for the Labor-held seat of Williamstown in Melbourne's west, over comments about Indigenous Australians that came to light on Wednesday.

In a statement, the party said the views Mr Lindemann had expressed were "offensive, unacceptable and inconsistent with the values and standards expected of Liberal candidates", the ABC reported. It said all candidates were expected to treat Australians with dignity and respect, that Mr Lindemann's comments "fell short of that standard", and that it had not previously been aware of them.

The Age reported that the comments were posted from an anonymous Facebook account, named after Mr Lindemann's yacht, that it linked to him. It reported that in posts about the proposed Voice to Parliament, the account described Indigenous Australians as "never civilised".
Earlier on Wednesday, Sport Minister Steve Dimopoulos called on Opposition Leader Jess Wilson to drop Mr Lindemann over his conduct as a junior basketball coach, the ABC reported.

Mr Lindemann was suspended for six weeks last year for bringing the game into disrepute after an under-14 girls' game, The Age and 7NEWS reported. He told The Age he had acted on his "first instinct" to protect a player. In a statement, he apologised and said he should have "handled the situation differently", according to the ABC.
Nominations for the 28 November election have closed, so Mr Lindemann's name will stay on the Williamstown ballot paper, The Age reported.

Labor has held Williamstown for all but four years since 1889. Jobs Minister Melissa Horne has held the seat since 2018, and kept it at the last election with a two-party-preferred margin of 13.4 per cent, The Age reported.
The decision came a day after One Nation dropped its Preston candidate, Franco Guardiani, over social media posts praising Adolf Hitler.

body: People applying for an Australian visa in India may now be asked to provide biometrics, meaning fingerprints and a facial image, as part of the application. The Australian High Commission in New Delhi announced the change from 26 October 2026.

The High Commission says India is one of nearly 60 countries where Australia is expanding biometric collection. The rule applies only to new applications lodged from 26 October; applications already submitted are not affected.
This matters for Melbourne families sponsoring or inviting parents, relatives and friends from India, such as for visitor visas.

ul: The Department of Home Affairs tells each applicant whether they need to provide biometrics, with instructions.
Depending on their circumstances, applicants may be asked to attend an Australian Biometrics Collection Centre in person.
Eligible applicants who have given biometrics at a collection centre before and hold a valid passport may be able to use the Australian Immi App instead, at no cost.
The High Commission says visa processing times are not expected to be affected.

body: The announcement does not list which visa types or age groups are covered. Applicants should follow the instructions they receive from Home Affairs.

body: The royal commission into corruption on Victoria's major infrastructure projects has heard that a two-day union stoppage at a Sunbury level crossing site in 2022 pushed up the project's costs by an estimated $6 million, and that the state paid for it.

"Practically speaking, every dollar spent at Gap Road was paid first by the state," counsel assisting Chris Young KC told the hearing in Collingwood on Monday, according to ABC News coverage. The first witnesses are due to give evidence from today, Tuesday 10 November.

body.note: Allegations aired at a royal commission are not proven. Mr Young said some of them have been denied. The commission has made no findings.

body.h: What the commission heard on day one

body: Mr Young said union officials repeatedly ordered work to stop on 6 and 7 June 2022, during a shutdown of the Sunbury line for critical works. Work resumed that evening after a meeting at the CFMEU's offices, without the safety issues that had been cited being fixed, he said. Union-backed health and safety representatives were appointed shortly afterwards.

A labour-hire firm engaged on the site in June 2022 went from two workers to 20 and billed about $1.2 million by September, the commission heard. That firm's licence has since been cancelled. CFMEU officials visited the site 34 times in a year, while WorkSafe inspectors recorded no breaches, Mr Young said.

The project's target cost rose from $110 million to $116 million after the stoppage. It was delivered for $104 million, which Mr Young said meant the alliance building it collected about $2 million in extra profit under its contract. He said other contractors had described "remarkably similar" experiences on other major projects, including North East Link, and that some agencies had been slow to hand over documents.

The hearing was also read a 2017 memo by contractor John Holland which said the CFMEU had "unprecedented access to ministers" and would probably know about government tenders before they were announced. Notes from a contractors' meeting recorded a threat that workers would be "smashed" if they turned up. Police and WorkSafe were notified, the commission heard, but no action was taken. These are claims recorded in documents, not findings.

Premier Ben Carroll denied knowing about the CFMEU's access to senior officials and ministers. "What today's hearings show is that I am a premier that will make the tough decisions," he said. He also confirmed the state would pay for lawyers for former premiers Jacinta Allan and Daniel Andrews at the inquiry. "I want to make sure Victorians get the answers they deserve," he said.

body.h: What the commission will look at

body: Mr Young set out themes the inquiry expects to explore. They include allegations that the union placed unelected delegates on sites as health and safety representatives, sometimes through labour-hire companies, and that contractors were often left to deal with disruption themselves by "buying peace" and pricing its cost into their bids. He said those costs were shared with the state or passed on to it.

He tendered a June 2023 briefing to Jacinta Allan, then the transport infrastructure minister, which raised concerns including pressure on contractors, excess staffing on sites, a rise in full-time union delegates and threats of unprotected industrial action. The briefing records concerns raised at the time and is not a finding. AAP has reported that Ms Allan, who later became premier, will be required to give evidence, but it is not yet known when.
Later hearing blocks will examine alleged links between organised crime and the construction industry, and how government money was allocated and projects chosen.
Mr Young also warned that threatening or punishing a witness is a serious offence, and said any reported threat would be referred to Victoria Police.

The Royal Commission into the Integrity of Major Public and Civil Infrastructure Construction Projects in Victoria was established on 20 August 2026. It is led by the Honourable Christopher Kourakis AC, a former chief justice of South Australia, and its final report is due by 20 August 2027.

Premier Ben Carroll called the inquiry as his first act after replacing Ms Allan, who had resisted calls from across the parliament for a royal commission. The calls followed reporting by Nine newspapers in 2024 alleging corruption and criminal infiltration of the CFMEU and Big Build sites. Parts of the union were placed into administration by the federal government in August 2024.

A report for the union's administrators by barrister Geoffrey Watson SC estimated that alleged corrupt conduct had effectively cost Victorian taxpayers $15 billion. That figure is Mr Watson's estimate, and testing claims like it is part of the commission's work.

This block of hearings runs until Friday 20 November, overlapping with early voting, which opens on Wednesday 18 November. Polling day is Saturday 28 November. A second block of hearings is expected before the end of the year, ABC News has reported.
ABC News has reported that the hearings will run through about two weeks of the four-week campaign. Mr Carroll has said that "integrity is not negotiable".

body: Two days into its first public hearings, Victoria's royal commission into corruption on major construction projects has looked at just one job: the removal of a level crossing at Gap Road, Sunbury, in 2022. But the documents and evidence aired in a Collingwood hearing room this week reach well beyond one rail bridge, to the questions of how much power the CFMEU held on Big Build sites, what that cost taxpayers, and how much the state knew.

None of it has been tested. The commission has made no findings, some of the allegations have been denied, and the union is represented at the hearing and has questioned witnesses. This block of hearings runs until Friday 20 November, two days after early voting opens, so the first early voters will cast their ballots while evidence is still being heard, and long before any findings are made.

body.note: Allegations and evidence at a royal commission are not proven. Documents read at the hearing record what their authors believed at the time. The commission's final report is not due until August 2027.

body.h: Five things the commission has heard

ul: One job, two days, $6 million. Counsel assisting Chris Young KC said a stoppage on 6 and 7 June 2022 pushed Gap Road's target cost from $110 million to $116 million, and that "every dollar" spent on the site was paid first by the state, according to ABC News. The project was eventually delivered for $104 million, which he said meant the alliance building it collected about $2 million in extra profit under its contract.

A worker says he 'had to' join. Crane operator Glenn Tyrrell, the site's elected health and safety representative, told the commission that union organisers would "come on site and literally stop the whole job", ABC News reported. He said about 15 casual workers were later called into a lunch room, told to move to a different labour-hire firm and told they had to join the CFMEU. He said he paid $590 up front for six months of union fees, the first time he had joined any union.

Safety was the stated reason, and the supervisor disputes it. John Holland site supervisor Robert Van Den Tol, giving evidence by video, said he had always considered the site safe and rejected the union's claim of a risk-assessment problem with piling work: "if I had seen it, I would have stopped it," he said, according to ABC News. He said he believed the union was targeting the project because it was the last crew in Melbourne without a union-affiliated safety representative. Under questioning from the CFMEU's lawyer, he agreed that a WorkSafe note about protection around deep holes appeared to be a valid complaint, NCA NewsWire reported.

The costs spread beyond one site. AAP reported that the site's traffic-control contractor was replaced four days after a closed-door meeting during the stoppage. The Guardian reported counsel as saying traffic controllers' rates rose from about $45 to $88 an hour, and that a government briefing to Jacinta Allan, then the minister responsible, estimated the union's campaign over traffic-management pay would add $60 million to $78 million to current projects and well over $400 million to projects being planned.

The paper trail reaches government. Internal documents from the contractor John Holland, read at the hearing, described the CFMEU as having "unprecedented access to ministers" and "a significant level of influence within the state government", AAP and The Guardian reported. These are a contractor's views, not findings. Counsel also tendered a June 2023 briefing to Ms Allan that raised concerns about pressure on contractors, excess staffing and a rise in full-time union delegates.

body.h: Gap Road, June 2022: the timeline so far

dl: The CFMEU issues eight safety notices to John Holland, ABC News reported. A further 23 notices follow on 1 and 2 June.
The project enters a planned 30-day shutdown of the Sunbury line.
Union officials stop work on the site.
A meeting is held at the CFMEU's offices. Work resumes afterwards, without the safety issues that had been cited being fixed, counsel said.
The traffic-control contractor is replaced (AAP). About a week after the stoppage, casual workers are told to change labour-hire firm and join the union (Mr Tyrrell's evidence).
Works are completed. The project comes in at $104 million against a revised target of $116 million.

body.h: What the union and the politicians say

body: The CFMEU's construction division has been in administration since the federal government intervened in August 2024. Its lawyers have cross-examined witnesses this week, but none of the reports we read carried a public response from the union or its administrators to the evidence. Administrator Michael Crosby has previously said developers, head contractors, subcontractors and labour-hire operators should also be called, ABC News reported.

The commission's own terms of reference exclude lawful industrial action and lawful actions under workplace safety laws. The question for the commissioner is whether conduct went beyond what the law allows.

Premier Ben Carroll, who announced the inquiry on the day he replaced Ms Allan as Labor leader in July, has said Victorians "deserve answers". His government is paying for lawyers for Ms Allan and former premier Daniel Andrews. Liberal leader Jess Wilson said that "doesn't pass the pub test", The Guardian reported.

Lawyers for Ms Allan and Mr Andrews attended Monday's hearing, and both are open to being called to give evidence, AAP reported. Counsel assisting has said notices will be issued to each person named in the 2023 briefing "in due course", The Nightly reported. No date has been announced.

body.h: The questions still to be answered

ul: How much did the state know? "We will examine how much the state knew and what it didn't," Commissioner Christopher Kourakis said on Monday, according to AAP.
Was Gap Road typical? Counsel said other contractors had described "remarkably similar" experiences on other major projects, including North East Link, ABC News reported.

Where does organised crime fit in? Counsel said apparently legitimate businesses had paid people linked to organised crime for services that appeared to involve "little more than intimidation and menace", AAP reported. Later hearing blocks will examine those links, and how government money was allocated and projects chosen.

Is anyone holding back? Counsel said some parties had not complied with notices to produce documents, in some cases citing government policy, The Guardian reported. He also said about half of the companies invited to make voluntary submissions had not responded, NCA NewsWire reported.

What did it all cost? A report for the union's administrators by barrister Geoffrey Watson SC estimated that alleged corrupt conduct had effectively cost Victorian taxpayers $15 billion. That is his estimate, and testing claims like it is part of the commission's job.

body: Judges would have to treat an attack on someone who steps in to help another person as an aggravating factor when sentencing, under a law the Victorian Coalition says it will introduce if it wins the state election on 28 November.

Opposition Leader Jess Wilson has named the proposal Aidan's Law, after Aidan Becker, a 22-year-old off-duty security guard who died after he was stabbed at Mernda railway station, in Melbourne's north, in March while trying to help a 14-year-old boy. Ms Wilson said the policy followed a request from Mr Becker's mother, Natalie, AAP reported.
"If you're brave enough to stand up for someone else, the law should stand up for you," Ms Wilson said.

Victorian courts can already take that kind of circumstance into account, but the law does not specifically require them to, according to AAP. Details such as wording, penalties and timing were not part of the announcement as reported.

body.note: Several people have been charged in connection with Mr Becker's death. The case is before the courts.

body.h: Labor's pitch on the same day

body: Premier Ben Carroll promised 200 more police reservists, former officers who would answer phones and staff counters at police stations, on top of 400 already being recruited. He also announced two new police stations and the rebuilding or upgrading of four others, AAP reported.
"Victorians have been very clear that they want to see someone at the counter when they walk into their local station," Mr Carroll said.
The Labor government has started a review of Victoria's sentencing laws, with public consultation due to begin in April 2027.
Early voting opens on Wednesday 18 November, and election day is Saturday 28 November.

body: More than $450,000 has been raised for the family of Feng Jianming, the food delivery rider killed near Queen Victoria Market on Friday night, as a Footscray man faced court charged with his murder.

Roberto Urbano, 51, of Footscray, has been charged with murder and intentionally causing serious injury. He appeared at Melbourne Magistrates' Court by video link on Monday and is due back in court on 26 April.

Mr Feng, 47, was a father of two from Shaanxi province in China who had lived in Australia for about nine years, the ABC reported. He was stabbed on Frederick Way at about 8pm on 6 November. A 34-year-old rider was seriously injured and taken to hospital.

body.note: This case is before the courts. The Melbourne Indian will not publish anything that could affect a fair trial.

body: The GoFundMe appeal was set up by the Melbourne Chinatown Business Association. Flowers have been left near the State Library.

body: Diwali falls on Sunday 8 November this year, the date set by the lunar calendar. For many Hindu, Sikh and Jain families in Melbourne, the day brings prayers, lamps, sweets and visits to family and friends.

Public celebrations started early. Melbourne Diwali, a free festival run by the not-for-profit SarasCare, was scheduled for Saturday 31 October at Marvel Stadium Square in Docklands, from 2pm to 10pm.

On Saturday 7 November the Immigration Museum on Flinders Street held a day of free Diwali activities, including henna, rangoli and traditional games. In ticketed Indian embroidery workshops, visitors added their own work to a shared 10-metre textile artwork.

Many Hindu temples and Sikh gurdwaras across Melbourne hold special prayers and services around Diwali. For Sikhs, the day is also Bandi Chhor Divas, which marks the release of Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji from imprisonment. Check with your local temple or gurdwara for times.

The next major date for many in the community is the Gurpurab of Guru Nanak Dev Ji later this month. Published calendars list it on 24 or 25 November, depending on the calendar and time zone used, so confirm the dates of nagar kirtans and services with your gurdwara.

body: चंद्र पंचांग के अनुसार इस साल दिवाली रविवार, 8 नवंबर को है। मेलबर्न में बहुत से हिंदू, सिख और जैन परिवारों के लिए यह दिन पूजा, दीयों, मिठाइयों और अपनों से मिलने-जुलने का दिन है।

सार्वजनिक उत्सव पहले ही शुरू हो गए थे। गैर-लाभकारी संस्था SarasCare द्वारा आयोजित निःशुल्क 'मेलबर्न दिवाली' उत्सव शनिवार, 31 अक्टूबर को डॉकलैंड्स के मार्वल स्टेडियम स्क्वेयर में दोपहर 2 बजे से रात 10 बजे तक होना तय था।

शनिवार, 7 नवंबर को फ़्लिंडर्स स्ट्रीट स्थित इमिग्रेशन म्यूज़ियम में दिवाली की निःशुल्क गतिविधियाँ हुईं, जिनमें मेहंदी, रंगोली और पारंपरिक खेल शामिल थे। टिकट वाली भारतीय कढ़ाई कार्यशालाओं में लोगों ने 10 मीटर लंबी साझा कपड़ा-कलाकृति में अपना योगदान जोड़ा।

दिवाली के आसपास मेलबर्न के कई हिंदू मंदिरों और सिख गुरुद्वारों में विशेष पूजा और दीवान होते हैं। सिखों के लिए यह दिन बंदी छोड़ दिवस भी है, जो गुरु हरगोबिंद साहिब जी की क़ैद से रिहाई की याद में मनाया जाता है। समय जानने के लिए अपने नज़दीकी मंदिर या गुरुद्वारे से संपर्क करें।

समुदाय में बहुतों के लिए अगली बड़ी तारीख़ इसी महीने गुरु नानक देव जी का प्रकाश पर्व (गुरपुरब) है। अलग-अलग कैलेंडर और समय-क्षेत्र के हिसाब से प्रकाशित पंचांगों में इसकी तारीख़ 24 या 25 नवंबर दी गई है, इसलिए नगर कीर्तन और दीवानों की तारीख़ अपने गुरुद्वारे से पक्की कर लें।

body: ਚੰਦਰ ਕੈਲੰਡਰ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਇਸ ਸਾਲ ਦੀਵਾਲੀ ਐਤਵਾਰ, 8 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਨੂੰ ਹੈ। ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਦੇ ਬਹੁਤ ਸਾਰੇ ਹਿੰਦੂ, ਸਿੱਖ ਅਤੇ ਜੈਨ ਪਰਿਵਾਰਾਂ ਲਈ ਇਹ ਦਿਨ ਅਰਦਾਸ-ਪੂਜਾ, ਦੀਵਿਆਂ, ਮਠਿਆਈਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਆਪਣਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਮਿਲਣ ਦਾ ਦਿਨ ਹੈ।

ਜਨਤਕ ਜਸ਼ਨ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਹੀ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਹੋ ਗਏ ਸਨ। ਗੈਰ-ਮੁਨਾਫ਼ਾ ਸੰਸਥਾ SarasCare ਵੱਲੋਂ ਕਰਵਾਇਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਮੁਫ਼ਤ 'ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਦੀਵਾਲੀ' ਮੇਲਾ ਸ਼ਨੀਵਾਰ, 31 ਅਕਤੂਬਰ ਨੂੰ ਡੌਕਲੈਂਡਜ਼ ਦੇ ਮਾਰਵਲ ਸਟੇਡੀਅਮ ਸਕੁਏਅਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਦੁਪਹਿਰ 2 ਵਜੇ ਤੋਂ ਰਾਤ 10 ਵਜੇ ਤੱਕ ਹੋਣਾ ਤੈਅ ਸੀ।

ਸ਼ਨੀਵਾਰ, 7 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਨੂੰ ਫ਼ਲਿੰਡਰਜ਼ ਸਟ੍ਰੀਟ ਸਥਿਤ ਇਮੀਗ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਨ ਮਿਊਜ਼ੀਅਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਦੀਵਾਲੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਮੁਫ਼ਤ ਗਤੀਵਿਧੀਆਂ ਹੋਈਆਂ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਹਿੰਦੀ, ਰੰਗੋਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਰਵਾਇਤੀ ਖੇਡਾਂ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਸਨ। ਟਿਕਟ ਵਾਲੀਆਂ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਕਢਾਈ ਵਰਕਸ਼ਾਪਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਨੇ 10 ਮੀਟਰ ਲੰਮੀ ਸਾਂਝੀ ਕੱਪੜਾ-ਕਲਾਕ੍ਰਿਤੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਪਣਾ ਹਿੱਸਾ ਪਾਇਆ।

ਦੀਵਾਲੀ ਦੇ ਆਸ-ਪਾਸ ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਦੇ ਕਈ ਹਿੰਦੂ ਮੰਦਰਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਖ਼ਾਸ ਪੂਜਾ ਅਤੇ ਦੀਵਾਨ ਸਜਦੇ ਹਨ। ਸਿੱਖਾਂ ਲਈ ਇਹ ਦਿਨ ਬੰਦੀ ਛੋੜ ਦਿਵਸ ਵੀ ਹੈ, ਜੋ ਗੁਰੂ ਹਰਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਕੈਦ ਤੋਂ ਰਿਹਾਈ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਨਾਇਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਸਮੇਂ ਲਈ ਆਪਣੇ ਨੇੜਲੇ ਮੰਦਰ ਜਾਂ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰੇ ਨਾਲ ਸੰਪਰਕ ਕਰੋ।

ਭਾਈਚਾਰੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਹੁਤਿਆਂ ਲਈ ਅਗਲੀ ਵੱਡੀ ਤਰੀਕ ਇਸੇ ਮਹੀਨੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ ਪੁਰਬ ਹੈ। ਵੱਖ-ਵੱਖ ਕੈਲੰਡਰਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਮਾਂ-ਖੇਤਰਾਂ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਛਪੀਆਂ ਜੰਤਰੀਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਇਸਦੀ ਤਰੀਕ 24 ਜਾਂ 25 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ, ਇਸ ਲਈ ਨਗਰ ਕੀਰਤਨ ਅਤੇ ਦੀਵਾਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਤਰੀਕ ਆਪਣੇ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰੇ ਤੋਂ ਪੱਕੀ ਕਰ ਲਓ।

body: When Prime Minister Anthony Albanese hosted Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the third Australia–India Annual Summit in Melbourne in July, the two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to a Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA). Modi said the two countries had decided to "work at a fast pace" on the CECA and on a bilateral investment treaty.

India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and Australia's Trade Minister Don Farrell discussed speeding up the negotiations when they met on the sidelines of the G20 trade ministers' meeting in Milwaukee on 30 September and 1 October, according to a post by Goyal. No timetable for concluding the agreement has been announced, The Indian Sun reported.

The interim Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (ECTA) has been in force since 29 December 2022. From 1 January 2026, eligible Indian goods gained duty-free access across all Australian tariff lines, subject to rules of origin.
India was Australia's sixth-largest trading partner in 2025, with two-way trade in goods and services worth A$50.2 billion, according to the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

ul: A Joint Declaration on Defence and Security Cooperation, and a new partnership on cyber, critical technologies and supply chains.

Approval for Melbourne's Victoria University to operate a campus in Gurugram, and a letter of intent for a Flinders University campus in Bengaluru.
$10 million for the Centre for Australia-India Relations' Maitri grants, which support business and people-to-people links.
A temporary space tracking terminal on the Cocos (Keeling) Islands to support India's Gaganyaan human spaceflight program.

body: India has overtaken England as the most common overseas country of birth for people living in Australia, according to Australian Bureau of Statistics figures released on 29 April 2026.

About 971,000 India-born people were living in Australia at 30 June 2025, with the England-born population also at about 971,000. India narrowly overtook England during 2025, the first time it has held the top position.

The India-born population also recorded the largest increase of any birthplace group since 2015, rising by 522,000. The Italy-born and England-born populations recorded the largest decreases over the same period.
Overall, 8.8 million people living in Australia, or 32 per cent of the population, were born overseas.

The milestone was noted in July, when Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met in Melbourne. Their joint statement said the Indian community in Australia was "now Australia's largest overseas-born group".

body: ऑस्ट्रेलियन ब्यूरो ऑफ़ स्टैटिस्टिक्स (ABS) के 29 अप्रैल 2026 को जारी आँकड़ों के अनुसार, ऑस्ट्रेलिया में रहने वालों के विदेशी जन्म-देश के रूप में भारत ने इंग्लैंड को पीछे छोड़ दिया है।

30 जून 2025 तक ऑस्ट्रेलिया में भारत में जन्मे लगभग 9 लाख 71 हज़ार लोग रह रहे थे, और इंग्लैंड में जन्मे लोगों की संख्या भी लगभग इतनी ही थी। 2025 के दौरान भारत मामूली अंतर से इंग्लैंड से आगे निकला, और यह पहली बार है जब भारत शीर्ष पर पहुँचा है।

2015 के बाद से किसी भी जन्म-देश समूह में सबसे बड़ी बढ़ोतरी भी भारत में जन्मे लोगों की रही, जिनकी संख्या 5 लाख 22 हज़ार बढ़ी। इसी अवधि में इटली और इंग्लैंड में जन्मे लोगों की संख्या में सबसे ज़्यादा गिरावट आई।
कुल मिलाकर ऑस्ट्रेलिया में रहने वाले 88 लाख लोग, यानी आबादी का 32 प्रतिशत, विदेश में जन्मे हैं।

2015 ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਜਨਮ-ਦੇਸ਼ ਸਮੂਹ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡਾ ਵਾਧਾ ਵੀ ਭਾਰਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਜੰਮੇ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਦਾ ਰਿਹਾ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ 5 ਲੱਖ 22 ਹਜ਼ਾਰ ਵਧੀ। ਇਸੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਇਟਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਇੰਗਲੈਂਡ ਵਿੱਚ ਜੰਮੇ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਧ ਕਮੀ ਆਈ।

body: Indian passport, visa and other consular applications in Australia are now handled through six VFS Global centres, in Adelaide, Brisbane, Canberra, Melbourne, Perth and Sydney, VFS Global said in July.

The Melbourne centre is on the ground floor of 324 St Kilda Road, Melbourne. Applicants book an appointment online through VFS Global's India–Australia portal. Applications are taken Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 4pm, except on public holidays and holidays declared by the Indian mission.
A VFS Global service charge of $115 per application applies from 23 July 2026, in addition to the Government of India fee, SBS Hindi reported, citing an announcement by the High Commission of India.

New passport and visa applications in Australia were suspended from 1 July while a dispute over the tender for India's outsourced consular services went through the Indian courts, Bloomberg reported. The High Commission of India in Canberra announced the restart on 23 July.

In May, SBS Hindi reported that India's Consul General in Melbourne, Anish Rajan, had announced a move from the Swanston Street office to a larger centre on St Kilda Road, with extra counters to shorten booking waits.

मेलबर्न केंद्र ग्राउंड फ़्लोर, 324 सेंट किल्डा रोड, मेलबर्न में है। आवेदकों को VFS ग्लोबल के भारत–ऑस्ट्रेलिया पोर्टल पर ऑनलाइन अपॉइंटमेंट बुक करनी होती है। आवेदन सोमवार से शुक्रवार, सुबह 8:30 से शाम 4 बजे तक जमा होते हैं, सार्वजनिक छुट्टियों और भारतीय मिशन द्वारा घोषित छुट्टियों को छोड़कर।
SBS हिंदी ने भारतीय उच्चायोग की घोषणा के हवाले से बताया कि 23 जुलाई 2026 से भारत सरकार के शुल्क के अलावा हर आवेदन पर $115 का VFS ग्लोबल सेवा शुल्क लगता है।

ब्लूमबर्ग के अनुसार, भारत की आउटसोर्स की गई कांसुलर सेवाओं के टेंडर को लेकर भारतीय अदालतों में चले विवाद के कारण 1 जुलाई से ऑस्ट्रेलिया में नए पासपोर्ट और वीज़ा आवेदन रोक दिए गए थे। कैनबरा स्थित भारतीय उच्चायोग ने 23 जुलाई को सेवाएँ फिर शुरू होने की घोषणा की।

मई में SBS हिंदी ने ख़बर दी थी कि मेलबर्न में भारत के महावाणिज्य दूत अनीश राजन ने स्वानस्टन स्ट्रीट कार्यालय की जगह सेंट किल्डा रोड पर एक बड़े केंद्र में जाने की घोषणा की है, जिसमें ज़्यादा काउंटर होंगे ताकि बुकिंग का इंतज़ार कम हो।

ul: अपॉइंटमेंट केवल ऑस्ट्रेलिया में भारतीय सेवाओं की आधिकारिक VFS ग्लोबल वेबसाइट से ही बुक करें।
अपॉइंटमेंट से पहले अपनी सेवा के लिए दस्तावेज़ों की ताज़ा सूची जाँच लें।

body: VFS ਗਲੋਬਲ ਨੇ ਜੁਲਾਈ ਵਿੱਚ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਕਿ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਪਾਸਪੋਰਟ, ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਅਤੇ ਹੋਰ ਕੌਂਸਲਰ ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ ਹੁਣ ਛੇ VFS ਗਲੋਬਲ ਕੇਂਦਰਾਂ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ: ਐਡੀਲੇਡ, ਬ੍ਰਿਸਬੇਨ, ਕੈਨਬਰਾ, ਮੈਲਬਰਨ, ਪਰਥ ਅਤੇ ਸਿਡਨੀ।

ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਗਰਾਊਂਡ ਫ਼ਲੋਰ, 324 ਸੇਂਟ ਕਿਲਡਾ ਰੋਡ, ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੈ। ਅਰਜ਼ੀਕਾਰਾਂ ਨੂੰ VFS ਗਲੋਬਲ ਦੇ ਭਾਰਤ–ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਪੋਰਟਲ 'ਤੇ ਆਨਲਾਈਨ ਅਪੌਇੰਟਮੈਂਟ ਬੁੱਕ ਕਰਨੀ ਪੈਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ ਸੋਮਵਾਰ ਤੋਂ ਸ਼ੁੱਕਰਵਾਰ, ਸਵੇਰੇ 8:30 ਤੋਂ ਸ਼ਾਮ 4 ਵਜੇ ਤੱਕ ਜਮ੍ਹਾਂ ਹੁੰਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ, ਸਰਕਾਰੀ ਛੁੱਟੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਮਿਸ਼ਨ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਐਲਾਨੀਆਂ ਛੁੱਟੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਛੱਡ ਕੇ।
SBS ਹਿੰਦੀ ਨੇ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਹਾਈ ਕਮਿਸ਼ਨ ਦੇ ਐਲਾਨ ਦੇ ਹਵਾਲੇ ਨਾਲ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਕਿ 23 ਜੁਲਾਈ 2026 ਤੋਂ ਭਾਰਤ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਦੀ ਫ਼ੀਸ ਤੋਂ ਇਲਾਵਾ ਹਰ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ 'ਤੇ $115 ਦੀ VFS ਗਲੋਬਲ ਸੇਵਾ ਫ਼ੀਸ ਲੱਗਦੀ ਹੈ।

ਬਲੂਮਬਰਗ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ, ਭਾਰਤ ਦੀਆਂ ਆਊਟਸੋਰਸ ਕੀਤੀਆਂ ਕੌਂਸਲਰ ਸੇਵਾਵਾਂ ਦੇ ਟੈਂਡਰ ਬਾਰੇ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਅਦਾਲਤਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਚੱਲੇ ਵਿਵਾਦ ਕਾਰਨ 1 ਜੁਲਾਈ ਤੋਂ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਵੀਆਂ ਪਾਸਪੋਰਟ ਅਤੇ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ ਰੋਕ ਦਿੱਤੀਆਂ ਗਈਆਂ ਸਨ। ਕੈਨਬਰਾ ਸਥਿਤ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਹਾਈ ਕਮਿਸ਼ਨ ਨੇ 23 ਜੁਲਾਈ ਨੂੰ ਸੇਵਾਵਾਂ ਮੁੜ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਹੋਣ ਦਾ ਐਲਾਨ ਕੀਤਾ।

ਮਈ ਵਿੱਚ SBS ਹਿੰਦੀ ਨੇ ਖ਼ਬਰ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਸੀ ਕਿ ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਭਾਰਤ ਦੇ ਕੌਂਸਲ ਜਨਰਲ ਅਨੀਸ਼ ਰਾਜਨ ਨੇ ਸਵਾਨਸਟਨ ਸਟ੍ਰੀਟ ਦਫ਼ਤਰ ਦੀ ਥਾਂ ਸੇਂਟ ਕਿਲਡਾ ਰੋਡ 'ਤੇ ਇੱਕ ਵੱਡੇ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਜਾਣ ਦਾ ਐਲਾਨ ਕੀਤਾ ਹੈ, ਜਿਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੱਧ ਕਾਊਂਟਰ ਹੋਣਗੇ ਤਾਂ ਜੋ ਬੁਕਿੰਗ ਦੀ ਉਡੀਕ ਘਟੇ।

ul: ਅਪੌਇੰਟਮੈਂਟ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਸੇਵਾਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਅਧਿਕਾਰਤ VFS ਗਲੋਬਲ ਵੈੱਬਸਾਈਟ ਤੋਂ ਹੀ ਬੁੱਕ ਕਰੋ।
ਅਪੌਇੰਟਮੈਂਟ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਆਪਣੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਲਈ ਦਸਤਾਵੇਜ਼ਾਂ ਦੀ ਤਾਜ਼ਾ ਸੂਚੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਲਓ।
ਵਾਧੂ ਸਮਾਂ ਰੱਖੋ, ਕਿਉਂਕਿ ਖ਼ਾਸ ਕਰਕੇ ਛੁੱਟੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਆਸ-ਪਾਸ ਅਪੌਇੰਟਮੈਂਟਾਂ ਦੀ ਉਪਲਬਧਤਾ ਬਦਲ ਸਕਦੀ ਹੈ।

body: The federal government has set the 2027 National Planning Level for new international student commencements at 295,000, unchanged from 2026, Study Australia announced in July.

The government says the planning level is not a cap on student numbers. Student visa applications are processed as a priority until a student's chosen provider reaches 80 per cent of its allocation. Applications after that point are still accepted but processed more slowly.
No active provider will receive a lower allocation in 2027 than in 2026, and TAFE students remain exempt from the planning level, The PIE News reported.

The student visa (subclass 500) application fee starts at A$2,500, according to the Department of Home Affairs. A lower fee applies to some applicants, including those enrolling in standalone English language (ELICOS) or non-award courses.
Education Minister Jason Clare said, as reported by The PIE News: "International education is an incredibly important export industry for Australia, but we need to manage it sustainably."

Melbourne's Victoria University received approval in July to open a campus in Gurugram, near Delhi. The university said the campus would teach through its block model, with students studying one subject at a time in four-week blocks, and that it was scheduled to open in August 2026.

body: Former Test opener Usman Khawaja has reopened one of Australian cricket's most painful episodes, writing in his new book, Sabr, that players and staff on the 2018 tour of South Africa knew about the ball-tampering plan that led to bans for three players.

David Warner, one of the three, backed Khawaja in a video on Instagram on Monday, calling his account "100 per cent accurate", the ABC reported. Warner also criticised Cricket Australia's 2018 investigation, saying Khawaja had not been interviewed and the process had been rushed.

Cricket Australia has consistently denied that all players and staff knew about the plan, according to the ABC. It is not yet known whether it will take any further action. Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft, the other two players banned in 2018, had not commented publicly at the time of writing.

Khawaja also writes about the Sheffield Shield. As reported by the ABC, he says Victorian teams of the 2000s and 2010s were probably the best at altering the ball, because the MCG pitch was flat and reverse swing and spin were the way to win there. He writes that he never tampered with a ball himself but knew what was going on and regarded himself as complicit.
Victoria and Australia fast bowler Scott Boland, speaking in Melbourne on Monday, said he had not seen anything untoward and that reverse swing had largely gone out of the game since 2018.
The row lands weeks before Australia's home Tests against New Zealand, and ahead of the tour of India from January. Khawaja's book is released on Tuesday 10 November.

body.note: The claims in this story are Usman Khawaja's, from his book as reported by the ABC. They have not been tested, and others named in the wider debate dispute them.

en.dek: Usman Khawaja writes that the whole touring party knew about the 2018 plan and that Victoria were the Shield's best at the 'dark arts'. Scott Boland says he has seen nothing untoward.

body: The City of Melbourne's 2026–27 budget includes more than $1.2 million to keep developing a Little India precinct in Docklands. The council's aim is a recognisable cultural destination alongside Chinatown and Koreatown, built through infrastructure, events and creative projects.

The funding was first flagged in the council's draft budget in March. Councillor Philip Le Liu said at the time, Melbourning reported: "As Australia's most multicultural city, we're taking big steps to make Little India a reality."

In its response to budget consultation, the council said it would focus on "testing future ideas for Little India". It has committed to engaging extensively with Docklands residents and Indian communities, and to running trial experiences so people can try ideas and help shape future plans.
More than 550 people contributed to the council's wider budget consultation, which ran from 31 March to 28 April.
No opening date has been announced. Lord Mayor Nick Reece discussed the project with SBS Hindi in May, and SBS reported that he had invited Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi to an official opening.

Local newspaper Docklands News reported that the council's consultation summary found a minority of submissions supported a Little India in Docklands, while most urged caution about a single-theme precinct. Concerns included top-down delivery and money being diverted from the suburb's other needs, with many residents pointing to greening, shade, wind protection and better public spaces.

The council has kept the $1.2 million commitment but is taking a staged approach that starts with trial activations, the paper reported. Council officers have said no exact location has been chosen, and the council has committed to finalising a Docklands public realm improvements plan.

At a budget hearing on 12 May, Federation of Indian Associations of Victoria president Vasan Srinivasan called the funding a "positive and historic beginning", but said a world-class precinct would need between $5 million and $10 million, Docklands News reported.

The proposal has also drawn what The Australia Today described in April as "negative and, at times, racist commentary". Mr Srinivasan launched a petition in support of the precinct, the outlet reported.
Victoria's strengthened anti-vilification laws, which added new civil protections from 15 April 2026, apply to public conduct online as well as offline.

en.dek: The City of Melbourne has set aside more than $1.2 million to develop a Little India precinct in Docklands, but no site has been chosen and many local residents have urged caution.

body: Community associations, temples, gurdwaras, cultural groups and trader associations can apply for Victorian Government funding, but most rounds open once a year and close within a few weeks. All three of the main 2026 programs below have now closed.

Grants ranged from $5,000 for smaller community events to $50,000 for events of any size, with a further $1 million set aside for events in rural and regional Victoria. Events had to be free, inclusive, accessible and culturally safe. Applications closed on 17 April 2026.

This $5 million program had three streams offering up to $10,000, $100,000 or $400,000 for skills, partnerships and leadership, and for day-to-day costs such as IT systems and business planning. Organisations from new and emerging communities, and from rural and regional areas, were a priority. Applications closed on 19 February 2026.

This fund offered $5,000 grants to not-for-profit business associations, such as trader groups and chambers of commerce, to run advice, training or mentoring for multicultural small business owners and their staff. Each project needed at least 10 participants. Applications closed at 4pm on 28 September 2026, and funded projects must be finished by 26 February 2027.

body: सामुदायिक संघ, मंदिर, गुरुद्वारे, सांस्कृतिक समूह और व्यापारी संघ विक्टोरियाई सरकार से फ़ंडिंग के लिए आवेदन कर सकते हैं, लेकिन ज़्यादातर दौर साल में एक बार खुलते हैं और कुछ ही हफ़्तों में बंद हो जाते हैं। नीचे दिए गए 2026 के तीनों मुख्य कार्यक्रम अब बंद हो चुके हैं।

छोटे सामुदायिक कार्यक्रमों के लिए $5,000 से लेकर किसी भी आकार के कार्यक्रम के लिए $50,000 तक के अनुदान थे, और ग्रामीण व क्षेत्रीय विक्टोरिया के कार्यक्रमों के लिए अलग से $1 मिलियन रखे गए। कार्यक्रमों का निःशुल्क, सबके लिए खुला, सुलभ और सांस्कृतिक रूप से सुरक्षित होना ज़रूरी था। आवेदन 17 अप्रैल 2026 को बंद हुए।

$5 मिलियन के इस कार्यक्रम में तीन श्रेणियाँ थीं, जिनमें कौशल, साझेदारी और नेतृत्व के लिए, और आईटी सिस्टम व व्यावसायिक योजना जैसे रोज़मर्रा के ख़र्चों के लिए $10,000, $100,000 या $400,000 तक मिल सकते थे। नए और उभरते समुदायों तथा ग्रामीण व क्षेत्रीय इलाक़ों के संगठनों को प्राथमिकता दी गई। आवेदन 19 फ़रवरी 2026 को बंद हुए।

इस कोष में गैर-लाभकारी व्यापार संघों, जैसे ट्रेडर समूहों और चैंबर ऑफ़ कॉमर्स, को $5,000 के अनुदान दिए गए, ताकि वे बहुसांस्कृतिक छोटे व्यवसायों के मालिकों और कर्मचारियों के लिए सलाह, प्रशिक्षण या मार्गदर्शन दे सकें। हर परियोजना में कम से कम 10 प्रतिभागी ज़रूरी थे। आवेदन 28 सितंबर 2026 को शाम 4 बजे बंद हुए, और स्वीकृत परियोजनाएँ 26 फ़रवरी 2027 तक पूरी करनी होंगी।

ul: सुनिश्चित करें कि आपके संगठन के पास वैध ABN हो और वह सही नियामक संस्था के पास पंजीकृत हो। व्यवसाय कौशल कोष के लिए दोनों ज़रूरी थे।

body: ਭਾਈਚਾਰਕ ਸਭਾਵਾਂ, ਮੰਦਰ, ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰੇ, ਸੱਭਿਆਚਾਰਕ ਗਰੁੱਪ ਅਤੇ ਵਪਾਰੀ ਸੰਘ ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਆ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਤੋਂ ਫ਼ੰਡਿੰਗ ਲਈ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦੇ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਬਹੁਤੇ ਗੇੜ ਸਾਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਇੱਕ ਵਾਰ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹਦੇ ਹਨ ਅਤੇ ਕੁਝ ਹਫ਼ਤਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੰਦ ਹੋ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਹੇਠਾਂ ਦਿੱਤੇ 2026 ਦੇ ਤਿੰਨੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ ਹੁਣ ਬੰਦ ਹੋ ਚੁੱਕੇ ਹਨ।

ਛੋਟੇ ਭਾਈਚਾਰਕ ਸਮਾਗਮਾਂ ਲਈ $5,000 ਤੋਂ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਆਕਾਰ ਦੇ ਸਮਾਗਮ ਲਈ $50,000 ਤੱਕ ਦੀਆਂ ਗ੍ਰਾਂਟਾਂ ਸਨ, ਅਤੇ ਪੇਂਡੂ ਤੇ ਖੇਤਰੀ ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਆ ਦੇ ਸਮਾਗਮਾਂ ਲਈ ਵੱਖਰੇ ਤੌਰ 'ਤੇ $1 ਮਿਲੀਅਨ ਰੱਖੇ ਗਏ। ਸਮਾਗਮਾਂ ਦਾ ਮੁਫ਼ਤ, ਸਾਰਿਆਂ ਲਈ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹਾ, ਪਹੁੰਚਯੋਗ ਅਤੇ ਸੱਭਿਆਚਾਰਕ ਤੌਰ 'ਤੇ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਅਤ ਹੋਣਾ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਸੀ। ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ 17 ਅਪ੍ਰੈਲ 2026 ਨੂੰ ਬੰਦ ਹੋਈਆਂ।

$5 ਮਿਲੀਅਨ ਦੇ ਇਸ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਤਿੰਨ ਸ਼੍ਰੇਣੀਆਂ ਸਨ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੁਨਰ, ਭਾਈਵਾਲੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਲੀਡਰਸ਼ਿਪ ਲਈ, ਅਤੇ ਆਈਟੀ ਸਿਸਟਮ ਤੇ ਕਾਰੋਬਾਰੀ ਯੋਜਨਾਬੰਦੀ ਵਰਗੇ ਰੋਜ਼ਾਨਾ ਖ਼ਰਚਿਆਂ ਲਈ $10,000, $100,000 ਜਾਂ $400,000 ਤੱਕ ਮਿਲ ਸਕਦੇ ਸਨ। ਨਵੇਂ ਅਤੇ ਉੱਭਰ ਰਹੇ ਭਾਈਚਾਰਿਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਪੇਂਡੂ ਤੇ ਖੇਤਰੀ ਇਲਾਕਿਆਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਸੰਸਥਾਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਪਹਿਲ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਗਈ। ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ 19 ਫ਼ਰਵਰੀ 2026 ਨੂੰ ਬੰਦ ਹੋਈਆਂ।

ਇਸ ਫ਼ੰਡ ਵਿੱਚ ਗੈਰ-ਮੁਨਾਫ਼ਾ ਵਪਾਰਕ ਸੰਘਾਂ, ਜਿਵੇਂ ਵਪਾਰੀ ਗਰੁੱਪਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਚੈਂਬਰ ਆਫ਼ ਕਾਮਰਸ, ਨੂੰ $5,000 ਦੀਆਂ ਗ੍ਰਾਂਟਾਂ ਦਿੱਤੀਆਂ ਗਈਆਂ, ਤਾਂ ਜੋ ਉਹ ਬਹੁ-ਸੱਭਿਆਚਾਰਕ ਛੋਟੇ ਕਾਰੋਬਾਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਮਾਲਕਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਮੁਲਾਜ਼ਮਾਂ ਲਈ ਸਲਾਹ, ਸਿਖਲਾਈ ਜਾਂ ਰਹਿਨੁਮਾਈ ਦੇ ਸਕਣ। ਹਰ ਪ੍ਰੋਜੈਕਟ ਵਿੱਚ ਘੱਟੋ-ਘੱਟ 10 ਭਾਗੀਦਾਰ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਸਨ। ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ 28 ਸਤੰਬਰ 2026 ਨੂੰ ਸ਼ਾਮ 4 ਵਜੇ ਬੰਦ ਹੋਈਆਂ, ਅਤੇ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰ ਪ੍ਰੋਜੈਕਟ 26 ਫ਼ਰਵਰੀ 2027 ਤੱਕ ਪੂਰੇ ਕਰਨੇ ਹੋਣਗੇ।

ul: ਯਕੀਨੀ ਬਣਾਓ ਕਿ ਤੁਹਾਡੀ ਸੰਸਥਾ ਕੋਲ ਚਾਲੂ ABN ਹੋਵੇ ਅਤੇ ਉਹ ਸਹੀ ਰੈਗੂਲੇਟਰ ਕੋਲ ਰਜਿਸਟਰਡ ਹੋਵੇ। ਕਾਰੋਬਾਰੀ ਹੁਨਰ ਫ਼ੰਡ ਲਈ ਦੋਵੇਂ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਸਨ।

body: One of Australia's biggest data centre companies has put the brakes on its growth after a fight with residents in Melbourne's inner west left its flagship West Footscray site short of power.

NEXTDC said on Monday it would pause all projects that do not have a customer contract, Reuters reported. Chief executive Craig Scroggie told a UBS investor conference the company "certainly didn't expect to be in the position we're in today", and linked the problem to public unease about artificial intelligence and data centres, which he described as an issue of "social license".
"That work can't restart until we clearly communicate that we've solved this problem," he said, adding that winning community support for the Melbourne site is now the top priority.

body.h: What went wrong in West Footscray

body: NEXTDC's M3 data centre sits about 10 kilometres west of the CBD and is planned to grow to 225 megawatts. To get more power, it needs electricity distributor Jemena to upgrade the local 66,000-volt network.

In September, Jemena stopped installing 15-metre power poles in neighbouring Yarraville after residents protested, with some leaving cars and bins out to block work crews, the ABC reported. Jemena cited community and stakeholder opposition, safety concerns and limited site access, and the local council has not given consent as road authority while consultation continues, according to NEXTDC. Jemena does not expect to resume before February 2027.

Residents have long raised concerns about diesel fumes and noise from the site, which they say is just 15 metres from homes. "NextDC M3 doesn't have social licence for the existing building, they certainly don't have it for an expansion," said Sean Brown, a founding member of residents' group Citizens of Tottenham. The group's president, Jacqui Glover, said the delay was "a reminder that the people living beside these developments cannot simply be pushed aside."

body: Goodman and Digital Realty said they had no current plans to make a takeover offer but reserved the right to do so. NEXTDC says construction is continuing inside the existing West Footscray buildings and the affected capacity is still under contract to an unnamed customer.

NEXTDC has applied to the Victorian Government to expand the site. The company says a decision on that permit is now expected in 2027 because of caretaker rules ahead of the 28 November state election. Victoria has also announced rules to keep new data centres at least 150 metres from homes and schools, the ABC reported.
NEXTDC is due to report the outcome of a review of its building plans at its annual general meeting on 20 November.

body: A Hindu temple in Melbourne's west was left without power on the eve of Diwali after its electricity was cut for the second time in eight days, according to MPs from both major parties. The incidents were first reported by The Indian Sun and South Asia Times.

Evan Mulholland, the Opposition's spokesman for multicultural and multifaith affairs, said power to the SMVS Swaminarayan temple in Mount Cottrell, next to Tarneit, was cut on Saturday 31 October, and the community paid thousands of dollars to have it reconnected. He said vandals returned on Saturday 7 November, the night before Diwali, and cut the power again at the main electrical board. The temple could not restore it in time for its celebrations, he said.
"No faith community in Victoria should have to live like this," Mr Mulholland said in a statement on Sunday, The Indian Sun reported.

body.note: The details of the power cuts come from MPs' statements. The Melbourne Indian has not been able to confirm them with Victoria Police, which had not commented publicly at the time of publication. No one has been charged and the motive is not known.

body: Tarneit's Labor MP, Dylan Wight, visited the temple on Sunday. He told The Indian Sun he was "deeply disappointed and concerned by the latest act of vandalism", and that no community should have to keep repairing damage to its place of worship.

Mr Wight also told the paper that Labor would provide $200,000 for security upgrades at the temple if it is re-elected on 28 November, with the work to be decided with temple management. How the money would be paid and when work could start have not been announced.

The Liberal candidate for Tarneit, Venkat Ram Upparlapalle, visited the temple last week and called for a thorough police investigation, stronger security and accountability. "A temple should be a place of peace, prayer and belonging," he wrote on social media.

Earlier this month Premier Ben Carroll announced an $11 million Temple and Gurdwara Safety Fund, for security and other upgrades at Hindu temples and Sikh gurdwaras, at the Sri Durga Temple in Deanside. South Asia Times reported that the Deanside temple would receive $1 million. The Melbourne Indian could not find a Coalition funding commitment for the SMVS temple at the time of publication.

Mr Mulholland said the temple had faced theft, break-ins, a firebombing, a vehicle being driven into the building and repeated interference with its power over more than a decade, sometimes before major festivals, The Indian Sun reported.

After a break-in before Holi in March 2025, temple trustee Biren Joshi told The Australia Today it was the eighth incident in eight years, and that no arrests had been made for any of them. The temple has received government money for security before: The Indian Sun reported that funding for fencing, gates and CCTV was set aside for it under the federal Safer Communities Fund in 2020.
Anyone with information can contact Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000 or at crimestoppersvic.com.au, and can stay anonymous. In an emergency, call triple zero (000).

body: Students hoping to come to Australia could have to move a large share of their course costs into an Australian bank account in their own name, and keep it there for up to three months, before they are even allowed to lodge a visa application, under options the federal government is now considering.

The Department of Home Affairs has released a consultation paper on changing the student visa's financial requirements and the Genuine Student test. No decision has been made, and the department says feedback will inform whether the reforms go ahead at all.

For Indian families, one part matters most. The paper floats an interim measure aimed at applicants from "Evidence Level 3" countries, the highest-scrutiny tier. India has been in that tier since 8 January this year, according to India's Minister of State for External Affairs, Kirti Vardhan Singh.

body.h: The four options on the table

dl: Half of all tuition and living costs for the whole course, in an Australian account for at least one month before lodging, released on a set schedule
Half of all course costs, held in an Australian account for at least three months, with no set release schedule
All tuition and living costs for the first 12 months, held in an Australian account for at least three months
Costs covered through recognised lenders, personal funds or both; moving money to an Australian account preferred where practical

body.h: What could change sooner for Indian applicants

body: While the longer-term rules are worked out, the paper proposes that every primary applicant from an Evidence Level 3 country would have to provide financial evidence when they lodge, whatever their university or college. The required amounts would stay the same at first, but deposits would need at least six months of transaction history.

Under the interim measure, money could generally come only from the applicant, a spouse, parents or another approved supporter. Unsecured personal loans, and loans that have not yet been paid out, would generally not be accepted.

body.h: How big could the numbers get?

body: The Department of Home Affairs changed the rules for Student visa (subclass 500) and Student Guardian visa (subclass 590) applications on 2 October 2026. The changes affect where people can apply from and whether family members can be included.

If you already hold a Student visa, the department says the changes do not affect your current visa. Applications lodged before 2 October, including those that listed family members, are assessed under the old rules.

According to the department's factsheet, most temporary visa holders in Australia can no longer lodge a Student or Student Guardian visa application while in Australia. This includes current Student visa holders applying for another Student visa, unless an exemption applies.
Current Student Guardian visa holders can still lodge a further Student Guardian visa application in Australia, the factsheet says.
If the new rules stop you applying onshore, you must be outside Australia both when you lodge the application and when the visa is granted.

body: New Student visa applicants can no longer include a partner or dependent children in their application unless an exemption applies. Exemptions include PhD students, students sponsored by DFAT or Defence, students on a foreign government scholarship, and eligible students from Pacific or ASEAN countries.

Current Student visa holders can no longer add family members after their visa is granted. The department says there are no exemptions to this rule. Family members already included on a current Student visa may be included in the next application if it is made in Australia.
The primary applicant and all family members in an application must be in the same location when it is lodged.

body: Victoria Police is investigating two incidents in which power cables were cut at the SMVS Swaminarayan temple in Melbourne's west in the days before Diwali, and is asking anyone with information or dashcam footage to come forward.

In a statement quoted by The Indian Sun on Monday, police said the incidents happened on 31 October and 6 November, and that the second also involved damage to a meter box. Police put the total damage at up to $8,000. The Hindu Council of Australia has said the second incident happened in the early hours of 7 November.
"It is yet to be determined if the offending were racially or religiously motivated," Victoria Police said, according to The Indian Sun. No one had been charged at the time of writing.

The temple's community and the Hindu Council have called for stronger security. Labor's member for Tarneit, Dylan Wight, has promised $200,000 for security at the temple if Labor is re-elected on 28 November. The Liberal candidate for Tarneit, Venkat Ram Upparlapalle, visited the temple and called for a thorough investigation, The Indian Sun reported.

ਸੋਮਵਾਰ ਨੂੰ The Indian Sun ਵੱਲੋਂ ਹਵਾਲਾ ਦਿੱਤੇ ਇੱਕ ਬਿਆਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੁਲਿਸ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ ਇਹ ਘਟਨਾਵਾਂ 31 ਅਕਤੂਬਰ ਅਤੇ 6 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਨੂੰ ਵਾਪਰੀਆਂ, ਅਤੇ ਦੂਜੀ ਘਟਨਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੀਟਰ ਬਾਕਸ ਦਾ ਵੀ ਨੁਕਸਾਨ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ। ਪੁਲਿਸ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਕੁੱਲ ਨੁਕਸਾਨ 8,000 ਡਾਲਰ ਤੱਕ ਦਾ ਹੈ। ਹਿੰਦੂ ਕੌਂਸਲ ਆਫ਼ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਦੂਜੀ ਘਟਨਾ 7 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਦੇ ਤੜਕੇ ਵਾਪਰੀ।

body: You will get two ballot papers. On the small lower house ballot paper, number every box in the order of your choice.

On the large upper house ballot paper, you can vote above the line for parties or groups, or below the line for individual candidates. Either way, number at least 1 to 5 in your order of choice. Use numbers only, not ticks or crosses.

body: Victorians go to the polls on Saturday 28 November for the 2026 state election. Voting centres will be open from 8am to 6pm, and you can vote at any voting centre in Victoria, according to the Victorian Electoral Commission (VEC).
Voting is compulsory for everyone on the electoral roll. The roll closed at 8pm on Tuesday 3 November, so if you are not sure whether you are enrolled, check your details on the VEC website.

dl: Early voting and telephone-assisted voting open

body: Early voting runs from Wednesday 18 to Friday 27 November, 9am to 6pm each day except Sunday 22 November. You do not need a reason to vote early. The VEC says early voting locations will be published closer to the date.
If you cannot get to a voting centre, you can apply for a postal vote until 6pm on Wednesday 25 November. Ballot packs are posted after nominations close and candidates are confirmed.
Telephone-assisted voting is available for people who are blind, have low vision or have a motor impairment. Registration opens on Wednesday 18 November.

The VEC publishes voting information in other languages on its website, and early and election-day voting centres have how-to-vote information in other languages. You can also call the VEC on 131 832.

body: विक्टोरिया के मतदाता 2026 के राज्य चुनाव के लिए शनिवार, 28 नवंबर को वोट डालेंगे। विक्टोरियन इलेक्टोरल कमीशन (VEC) के अनुसार मतदान केंद्र सुबह 8 बजे से शाम 6 बजे तक खुले रहेंगे, और आप विक्टोरिया के किसी भी मतदान केंद्र पर वोट दे सकते हैं।

मतदाता सूची में दर्ज हर व्यक्ति के लिए मतदान अनिवार्य है। मतदाता सूची मंगलवार, 3 नवंबर को रात 8 बजे बंद हो चुकी है। अगर आपको पक्का नहीं पता कि आपका नाम दर्ज है, तो VEC की वेबसाइट पर अपनी जानकारी जाँच लें।

body: अग्रिम मतदान बुधवार 18 नवंबर से शुक्रवार 27 नवंबर तक रोज़ सुबह 9 बजे से शाम 6 बजे तक होगा, केवल रविवार 22 नवंबर को छोड़कर। पहले वोट देने के लिए कोई कारण बताने की ज़रूरत नहीं है। VEC के अनुसार अग्रिम मतदान केंद्रों की जगहें तारीख़ के क़रीब बताई जाएँगी।
अगर आप मतदान केंद्र तक नहीं जा सकते, तो बुधवार 25 नवंबर शाम 6 बजे तक डाक मत के लिए आवेदन कर सकते हैं। नामांकन बंद होने और उम्मीदवार तय होने के बाद मतपत्र डाक से भेजे जाते हैं।
जो लोग देख नहीं सकते, कम देख पाते हैं या जिन्हें हाथ-पैर चलाने में कठिनाई है, वे टेलीफ़ोन की सहायता से वोट दे सकते हैं। इसका पंजीकरण बुधवार 18 नवंबर से शुरू होगा।
VEC अपनी वेबसाइट पर दूसरी भाषाओं में मतदान की जानकारी देता है, और अग्रिम व चुनाव-दिवस के मतदान केंद्रों पर भी दूसरी भाषाओं में वोट डालने की जानकारी मिलती है। आप VEC को 131 832 पर फ़ोन भी कर सकते हैं।

ਵੋਟਰ ਸੂਚੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਰਜ ਹਰ ਵਿਅਕਤੀ ਲਈ ਵੋਟ ਪਾਉਣੀ ਲਾਜ਼ਮੀ ਹੈ। ਵੋਟਰ ਸੂਚੀ ਮੰਗਲਵਾਰ, 3 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਨੂੰ ਰਾਤ 8 ਵਜੇ ਬੰਦ ਹੋ ਚੁੱਕੀ ਹੈ। ਜੇ ਤੁਹਾਨੂੰ ਪੱਕਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਪਤਾ ਕਿ ਤੁਹਾਡਾ ਨਾਂ ਦਰਜ ਹੈ ਜਾਂ ਨਹੀਂ, ਤਾਂ VEC ਦੀ ਵੈੱਬਸਾਈਟ 'ਤੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਵੇਰਵੇ ਜਾਂਚ ਲਓ।

dl: ਘੱਟ ਰੌਲੇ-ਰੱਪੇ ਵਾਲਾ (ਲੋ ਸੈਂਸਰੀ) ਵੋਟਿੰਗ ਸੈਸ਼ਨ

body: ਅਗਾਊਂ ਵੋਟਿੰਗ ਬੁੱਧਵਾਰ 18 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਤੋਂ ਸ਼ੁੱਕਰਵਾਰ 27 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਤੱਕ ਹਰ ਰੋਜ਼ ਸਵੇਰੇ 9 ਵਜੇ ਤੋਂ ਸ਼ਾਮ 6 ਵਜੇ ਤੱਕ ਹੋਵੇਗੀ, ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਐਤਵਾਰ 22 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਨੂੰ ਛੱਡ ਕੇ। ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਵੋਟ ਪਾਉਣ ਲਈ ਕੋਈ ਕਾਰਨ ਦੱਸਣ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਨਹੀਂ। VEC ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਅਗਾਊਂ ਵੋਟਿੰਗ ਕੇਂਦਰਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਥਾਵਾਂ ਤਰੀਕ ਦੇ ਨੇੜੇ ਦੱਸੀਆਂ ਜਾਣਗੀਆਂ।
ਜੇ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਵੋਟਿੰਗ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾ ਸਕਦੇ, ਤਾਂ ਬੁੱਧਵਾਰ 25 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਸ਼ਾਮ 6 ਵਜੇ ਤੱਕ ਡਾਕ ਵੋਟ ਲਈ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦੇ ਸਕਦੇ ਹੋ। ਨਾਮਜ਼ਦਗੀਆਂ ਬੰਦ ਹੋਣ ਅਤੇ ਉਮੀਦਵਾਰ ਪੱਕੇ ਹੋਣ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਬੈਲਟ ਪੇਪਰ ਡਾਕ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਭੇਜੇ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਹਨ।
ਜਿਹੜੇ ਲੋਕ ਦੇਖ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਕਦੇ, ਘੱਟ ਦੇਖਦੇ ਹਨ ਜਾਂ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਹੱਥਾਂ-ਪੈਰਾਂ ਦੀ ਹਿਲਜੁਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਿੱਕਤ ਹੈ, ਉਹ ਫ਼ੋਨ ਦੀ ਸਹਾਇਤਾ ਨਾਲ ਵੋਟ ਪਾ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਨ। ਇਸ ਲਈ ਰਜਿਸਟ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਨ ਬੁੱਧਵਾਰ 18 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਤੋਂ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਹੋਵੇਗੀ।

VEC ਆਪਣੀ ਵੈੱਬਸਾਈਟ 'ਤੇ ਹੋਰ ਬੋਲੀਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੋਟਿੰਗ ਦੀ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਅਤੇ ਅਗਾਊਂ ਅਤੇ ਚੋਣਾਂ ਵਾਲੇ ਦਿਨ ਦੇ ਵੋਟਿੰਗ ਕੇਂਦਰਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੀ ਹੋਰ ਬੋਲੀਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੋਟ ਪਾਉਣ ਦੀ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਹੈ। ਤੁਸੀਂ VEC ਨੂੰ 131 832 'ਤੇ ਫ਼ੋਨ ਵੀ ਕਰ ਸਕਦੇ ਹੋ।

body: Victoria's prisons were running at 92 per cent of capacity at the start of November, the ABC reported on Monday, as both major parties campaign on tougher bail, sentencing and policing ahead of the state election on 28 November.

According to the ABC, 4,624 people were serving sentences in Victorian prisons and 3,268 were on remand, meaning they were in custody waiting for a trial or a bail decision. By our arithmetic, that puts about four in ten prisoners on remand.

dl: A Labor spokesperson told the ABC the government had added more than 1,200 prison beds and recruited about 1,200 more prison officers, with $727 million set aside in the 2025-26 budget. Labor is also promising police station upgrades and a new rehabilitation program in youth detention.

Shadow police and corrections minister Brad Battin said a Coalition government would work with Corrections Victoria to manage prisoner numbers within the existing prisons. The Coalition is promising 1,500 more police on top of Labor's recruitment target.

Greens leader Ellen Sandell said the major parties were in "an arms race over who can lock up the most people", and called for more spending on mental health, drug and alcohol treatment and youth programs.

body: The ABC said neither major party answered its questions about whether it had planned for extra prison beds and staff, or what that would cost.

Arie Freiberg, a former long-serving chair of the Sentencing Advisory Council, told the ABC that tougher policies would push more people into police cells and that health and addiction services were a better investment than prisons. Swinburne University law professor Mirko Bagaric argued the opposite: that sentencing had been too lenient and more prisons would be money well spent.

The new Western Plains prison near Lara, which the ABC says cost $1.19 billion, has 1,292 maximum-security beds but is currently operating with capacity for 1,094. Port Phillip Prison in Truganina closed in 2025. The ABC estimates a new prison would cost more than $1 billion.

body.note: Figures in this story are as reported by the ABC. We have asked for the latest official data and will update this story.

en.dek: With law and order at the centre of the 28 November election, experts say neither Labor nor the Coalition has said how many extra prison beds their policies will need, or what they will cost.

हमारा ध्यान यहाँ की ज़िंदगी पर है: काउंसिल और राज्य सरकार के फ़ैसले, स्थानीय व्यवसाय, त्योहार और आस्था, और परिवारों के काम की व्यावहारिक जानकारी। भारत की ख़बरें तब छपेंगी जब उनका असर मेलबर्न में रहने वालों पर पड़ता हो।
हर ख़बर पढ़ने के लिए निःशुल्क है। हम अंग्रेज़ी, हिंदी और पंजाबी में प्रकाशित करते हैं, और जहाँ किसी भाषा में ख़बर पाठकों के काम आए, वहाँ उसका अनुवाद करते हैं।

हम प्रकाशित रिकॉर्ड और आधिकारिक स्रोतों से रिपोर्ट करते हैं, और हर ख़बर के अंत में उनके लिंक देते हैं ताकि आप ख़ुद जाँच सकें। शोध, लेखन और अनुवाद में हम AI टूल्स की मदद लेते हैं। हर ख़बर स्रोतों से मिलाई जाती है और प्रकाशन से पहले एक संपादक उसे मंज़ूरी देता है। राजनीति, अपराध, अदालत और लोगों पर लगे आरोपों जैसी संवेदनशील ख़बरों की अतिरिक्त जाँच होती है।

हमारा ख़र्च स्थानीय व्यवसायों के विज्ञापनों से चलता है। विज्ञापन और प्रायोजित सामग्री पर हमेशा स्पष्ट लेबल होता है, और वे यह तय नहीं करते कि हम क्या रिपोर्ट करें।

ਸਾਡਾ ਧਿਆਨ ਇੱਥੋਂ ਦੀ ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ 'ਤੇ ਹੈ: ਕੌਂਸਲ ਅਤੇ ਸੂਬਾ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਦੇ ਫ਼ੈਸਲੇ, ਸਥਾਨਕ ਕਾਰੋਬਾਰ, ਤਿਉਹਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਆਸਥਾ, ਅਤੇ ਪਰਿਵਾਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਕੰਮ ਆਉਣ ਵਾਲੀ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ। ਭਾਰਤ ਦੀਆਂ ਖ਼ਬਰਾਂ ਉਦੋਂ ਛਪਣਗੀਆਂ ਜਦੋਂ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦਾ ਅਸਰ ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਰਹਿਣ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ 'ਤੇ ਪੈਂਦਾ ਹੋਵੇ।

ਅਸੀਂ ਛਪੇ ਹੋਏ ਰਿਕਾਰਡਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਰਕਾਰੀ ਸਰੋਤਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਰਿਪੋਰਟ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਾਂ, ਅਤੇ ਹਰ ਖ਼ਬਰ ਦੇ ਅਖ਼ੀਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਲਿੰਕ ਦਿੰਦੇ ਹਾਂ ਤਾਂ ਜੋ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਆਪ ਜਾਂਚ ਕਰ ਸਕੋ। ਖੋਜ, ਲਿਖਾਈ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੁਵਾਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਅਸੀਂ AI ਟੂਲਾਂ ਦੀ ਮਦਦ ਲੈਂਦੇ ਹਾਂ। ਹਰ ਖ਼ਬਰ ਸਰੋਤਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲਾਈ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਛਪਣ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਕੋਈ ਸੰਪਾਦਕ ਉਸਨੂੰ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਸਿਆਸਤ, ਜੁਰਮ, ਅਦਾਲਤਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਲੋਕਾਂ 'ਤੇ ਲੱਗੇ ਦੋਸ਼ਾਂ ਵਰਗੀਆਂ ਸੰਵੇਦਨਸ਼ੀਲ ਖ਼ਬਰਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਾਧੂ ਜਾਂਚ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ।
ਅਸੀਂ ਕੋਈ ਹਵਾਲਾ, ਇੰਟਰਵਿਊ ਜਾਂ ਤਸਵੀਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਘੜਦੇ। ਗ਼ਲਤੀ ਹੋਣ 'ਤੇ ਅਸੀਂ ਉਸਨੂੰ ਸੁਧਾਰਦੇ ਹਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਫ਼ ਦੱਸਦੇ ਹਾਂ।
ਸਾਡਾ ਖ਼ਰਚਾ ਸਥਾਨਕ ਕਾਰੋਬਾਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਇਸ਼ਤਿਹਾਰਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਚੱਲਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇਸ਼ਤਿਹਾਰਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਪਾਂਸਰ ਕੀਤੀ ਸਮੱਗਰੀ 'ਤੇ ਹਮੇਸ਼ਾ ਸਾਫ਼ ਲੇਬਲ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਅਤੇ ਇਹ ਤੈਅ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰਦੇ ਕਿ ਅਸੀਂ ਕੀ ਰਿਪੋਰਟ ਕਰੀਏ।

body: At 11am today, Melbourne will pause for a minute. The Victorian State Remembrance Service begins at 10.30am at the Shrine of Remembrance, and anyone can attend without booking. For most Australians, the minute's silence brings to mind the diggers of Gallipoli and the Western Front. Fewer know that the men beside them in the trenches included thousands of soldiers from what was then undivided India.

Speaking at the Anzac Day dawn service in New Delhi this year, Australia's High Commissioner to India, Philip Green, put the number at around 16,000 troops from India who served at Gallipoli, with around 1,600 of them dying there. Sikh, Punjabi Muslim and Gurkha soldiers fought in battles such as Chunuk Bair and Hill 60, and Indian muleteers, stretcher-bearers and medical orderlies carried supplies under fire and tended the wounded.

Mr Green cited the historian Peter Stanley, who has argued that the Indian contribution at Gallipoli was as great as that of the ANZACs themselves. Photographs held by the Australian War Memorial show Indian soldiers on the landing beach at Anzac Cove, Indian gunners beside an Australian rest camp, and Indian mule teams camped at the head of what the diggers called Mule Gully.

The Australians noticed. In a letter home in 1915, Private Charlie Beherendt wrote that he had been "fighting side by side with Kitchener's army, and the Sikhs and Gurkhas", adding: "The Indians fight like tigers and are a great unit to the Empire."

body.h: The Indian Australians who enlisted anyway

body: Australia's Defence Act of 1909 said that people "not substantially of European origin or descent" were not eligible to enlist. Even so, the Australian War Memorial has identified at least 12 Indian Australians who joined the Australian Imperial Force in the First World War.

Two of them never came home. Nain Singh Sailani was born in Shimla and came to Western Australia in 1895, working as a labourer in Perth. He enlisted in February 1916, at the age of 43, and joined the 44th Battalion on the Western Front. He was killed on 1 June 1917 during a trench raid in Belgium and is buried at Strand Military Cemetery.

Sarn Singh came from Jullundur in Punjab and farmed near Loxton in South Australia's Riverland. He enlisted in May 1916, at about 38, and joined the 43rd Battalion. He was killed on 10 June 1917 during the advance on Messines Ridge, when enemy artillery struck his position.

A third, Desanda Singh of Kapurthala, a travelling salesman who settled near Ceduna, served with the 3rd Light Horse in Egypt in 1918 and came home. He was still working as a hawker in South Australia in 1946.

In July this year, the Commonwealth War Graves Commission added 9,909 Indian Army servicemen of the First World War to its official casualty records, the largest single addition since the Second World War. Most had died in India, away from the fighting fronts, and rulings by the British Indian government at the time denied them war-graves status, so their names were never passed on.

The names were recovered from the Punjab Registers, held at the Lahore Museum, which record the service of about 320,000 Punjabi recruits. The five-year project was run by the CWGC with the UK Punjab Heritage Association and the University of Greenwich. The men are now listed in an online book of remembrance, and families can search for them by name on the CWGC website.
"The recovery of every one of these 9,909 names helps restore missing chapters in family and world histories," the commission's director general, Claire Horton, said at the time.

The Victorian State Remembrance Service starts at 10.30am at the Second World War Memorial Forecourt of the Shrine of Remembrance, on St Kilda Road. No booking is needed, though seating is limited, and the service is also streamed online. At 11am the Shrine's Ray of Light falls on the word "Love" on the Stone of Remembrance, marking the moment the Armistice was signed in 1918; the public can see the alignment again at midday. Veterans, war widows and widowers travel free on public transport today.

body.note: The Gallipoli figures are the Australian High Commissioner's and are described as approximate. The Australian War Memorial says at least 12 Indian Australians enlisted; the true number may be higher, because some enlisted under anglicised names.

en.dek: Around 16,000 soldiers from India served at Gallipoli in 1915, and at least 12 Indian Australians joined the AIF despite a law that said they couldn't. This year, nearly 10,000 more Indian soldiers of the First World War were finally added to the official records.

body: Opposition Leader Jess Wilson has confirmed the Coalition will put Labor, the Greens and the Socialists at the bottom of its how-to-vote cards for the 28 November state election, which means One Nation will be ranked above them where it is standing.

"We have made the decision that we will be putting Labor, the Greens, the Socialists at the bottom of the ticket," Ms Wilson said on Tuesday, according to the ABC. "The only way to change the government is a number one next to Liberal and Nationals."

She said the order would be decided case by case, electorate by electorate, after checking each candidate. The Coalition has not yet said which seats will see One Nation placed directly after its own candidate.
The confirmation follows a report in The Australian on Monday that the Nationals had already resolved to preference One Nation ahead of Labor and that the Liberals were expected to follow.

Labor minister Anthony Carbines said Labor's position was "very clear about putting One Nation at the bottom", and accused the Coalition and One Nation of "nudge-nudge wink-wink" arrangements, the ABC reported. Premier Ben Carroll called the announcement a reversal of Ms Wilson's earlier position, The Australia Today reported.

On Wednesday, federal Labor MP Julian Hill, the member for Bruce, called it a deal between the two parties: "If it looks like a duck and quacks like a duck, it's a duck." Federal Liberal MP Aaron Violi, the member for Casey, said he was "comfortable" with the decision. "The preference recommendations are not making judgement calls on every single comment, policy or portfolio," he said.
One Nation welcomed the decision, The Australia Today reported. On the same day, the party dropped its candidate for Preston over social media posts praising Adolf Hitler.

Labor is facing criticism of its own. It will not direct preferences in the Liberal-held seat of Prahran, where it has previously preferenced the Greens, the ABC reported. Greens leader Ellen Sandell called the decision "shocking". "This is Labor admitting that they have more in common with One Nation and the Liberals," she said.

Victoria uses full preferential voting in the lower house: you must number every box. Parties hand out how-to-vote cards suggesting an order, and many voters follow them, so where each party asks its supporters to put its rivals can decide close seats once first preferences are counted.

body.note: Your vote is yours. How-to-vote cards are only suggestions: you can number the boxes in any order you choose, as long as every box is numbered.

body: From Thursday 12 November, people must be outside Australia both when they apply for a Training visa (subclass 407) and when it is granted, according to the Department of Home Affairs.
The 407 visa lets people come to Australia for workplace-based training or professional development with an approved sponsor.

ul: An application made while you are in Australia on or after 12 November will be invalid, Home Affairs says, "even if ImmiAccount allows you to submit an application".
A decision that an application is invalid cannot be reviewed on its merits.
Home Affairs warns that lodging an invalid application may affect your visa status, and that if your visa has already expired you may not be eligible to apply for another.
You will not get a Bridging visa linked to a 407 application lodged from outside Australia. You may travel to Australia on another valid visa while it is processed.

body: Home Affairs says valid applications lodged before 12 November will be assessed under the rules in place when they were lodged, including the changes that started on 11 March 2026. Since March, applicants have had to wait until their sponsor is approved and their training nomination is approved before applying, unless the sponsor is a Commonwealth agency.

ul: Check when your current visa expires and leave Australia before it does.
Make sure the sponsorship and nomination are approved before you apply.
Check whether you can do any health examination before you leave.
Do not book travel back to Australia based on an expected grant date.

body: The department has not published a reason for the change.

body.note: This is general information from the Department of Home Affairs, not migration advice. For advice on your situation, speak to a registered migration agent or lawyer.

body: गृह मामलों के विभाग (Department of Home Affairs) के अनुसार, गुरुवार 12 नवंबर से ट्रेनिंग वीज़ा (सबक्लास 407) के लिए आवेदन करते समय और वीज़ा मिलते समय, दोनों बार आवेदक का ऑस्ट्रेलिया से बाहर होना ज़रूरी होगा।
407 वीज़ा के ज़रिए लोग किसी मान्यता प्राप्त स्पॉन्सर के साथ कार्यस्थल पर आधारित ट्रेनिंग या प्रोफ़ेशनल डेवलपमेंट के लिए ऑस्ट्रेलिया आ सकते हैं।

ul: Home Affairs का कहना है कि 12 नवंबर या उसके बाद ऑस्ट्रेलिया में रहते हुए किया गया आवेदन अमान्य (invalid) होगा, "भले ही ImmiAccount आपको आवेदन जमा करने दे"।
किसी आवेदन को अमान्य ठहराने के फ़ैसले की मेरिट के आधार पर समीक्षा (review) नहीं हो सकती।

Home Affairs चेतावनी देता है कि अमान्य आवेदन जमा करने से आपके वीज़ा स्टेटस पर असर पड़ सकता है, और अगर आपका वीज़ा पहले ही ख़त्म हो चुका है तो हो सकता है कि आप दूसरे वीज़ा के लिए आवेदन करने के योग्य न रहें।
ऑस्ट्रेलिया के बाहर से किए गए 407 आवेदन से जुड़ा ब्रिजिंग वीज़ा नहीं मिलेगा। आवेदन पर कार्रवाई के दौरान आप किसी दूसरे मान्य वीज़ा पर ऑस्ट्रेलिया आ सकते हैं।

body: Home Affairs के अनुसार, 12 नवंबर से पहले जमा किए गए मान्य आवेदनों का आकलन उन्हीं नियमों के तहत होगा जो आवेदन के समय लागू थे, जिनमें 11 मार्च 2026 से लागू हुए बदलाव भी शामिल हैं। मार्च से आवेदकों को आवेदन करने से पहले अपने स्पॉन्सर और अपने ट्रेनिंग नॉमिनेशन, दोनों की मंज़ूरी का इंतज़ार करना पड़ता है, सिवाय तब जब स्पॉन्सर कोई कॉमनवेल्थ एजेंसी हो।

ul: देखें कि आपका मौजूदा वीज़ा कब ख़त्म हो रहा है, और उससे पहले ऑस्ट्रेलिया छोड़ दें।
आवेदन करने से पहले पक्का कर लें कि स्पॉन्सरशिप और नॉमिनेशन मंज़ूर हो चुके हैं।
पता करें कि क्या आप जाने से पहले कोई ज़रूरी मेडिकल जाँच करवा सकते हैं।
वीज़ा मिलने की अनुमानित तारीख़ के भरोसे ऑस्ट्रेलिया वापसी की यात्रा बुक न करें।

body: विभाग ने इस बदलाव का कोई कारण प्रकाशित नहीं किया है।

body.note: यह Department of Home Affairs की सामान्य जानकारी है, माइग्रेशन सलाह नहीं। अपनी स्थिति के बारे में सलाह के लिए किसी पंजीकृत माइग्रेशन एजेंट या वकील से बात करें।

body: ਗ੍ਰਹਿ ਮਾਮਲਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਵਿਭਾਗ (Department of Home Affairs) ਮੁਤਾਬਕ, ਵੀਰਵਾਰ 12 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਤੋਂ ਟ੍ਰੇਨਿੰਗ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ (ਸਬਕਲਾਸ 407) ਲਈ ਅਪਲਾਈ ਕਰਦੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਅਤੇ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਮਿਲਣ ਸਮੇਂ, ਦੋਵੇਂ ਵਾਰ ਬਿਨੈਕਾਰ ਦਾ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਹਰ ਹੋਣਾ ਲਾਜ਼ਮੀ ਹੋਵੇਗਾ।
407 ਵੀਜ਼ੇ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਲੋਕ ਕਿਸੇ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰਸ਼ੁਦਾ ਸਪਾਂਸਰ ਨਾਲ ਕੰਮ ਵਾਲੀ ਥਾਂ 'ਤੇ ਟ੍ਰੇਨਿੰਗ ਜਾਂ ਪ੍ਰੋਫ਼ੈਸ਼ਨਲ ਡਿਵੈਲਪਮੈਂਟ ਲਈ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਆ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਨ।

ul: Home Affairs ਦਾ ਕਹਿਣਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ 12 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਜਾਂ ਉਸ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਰਹਿੰਦਿਆਂ ਕੀਤੀ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਅਯੋਗ (invalid) ਹੋਵੇਗੀ, "ਭਾਵੇਂ ImmiAccount ਤੁਹਾਨੂੰ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਜਮ੍ਹਾਂ ਕਰਨ ਦੇਵੇ"।
ਕਿਸੇ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਨੂੰ ਅਯੋਗ ਠਹਿਰਾਉਣ ਦੇ ਫ਼ੈਸਲੇ ਦੀ ਮੈਰਿਟ ਦੇ ਆਧਾਰ 'ਤੇ ਸਮੀਖਿਆ (review) ਨਹੀਂ ਹੋ ਸਕਦੀ।

Home Affairs ਚਿਤਾਵਨੀ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਅਯੋਗ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਜਮ੍ਹਾਂ ਕਰਨ ਨਾਲ ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਸਟੇਟਸ 'ਤੇ ਅਸਰ ਪੈ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ, ਅਤੇ ਜੇ ਤੁਹਾਡਾ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਹੀ ਖ਼ਤਮ ਹੋ ਚੁੱਕਾ ਹੈ ਤਾਂ ਹੋ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਵੀਜ਼ੇ ਲਈ ਅਪਲਾਈ ਕਰਨ ਦੇ ਯੋਗ ਨਾ ਰਹੋ।
ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਹਰੋਂ ਕੀਤੀ 407 ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਿਆ ਬ੍ਰਿਜਿੰਗ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਮਿਲੇਗਾ। ਅਰਜ਼ੀ 'ਤੇ ਕਾਰਵਾਈ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਯੋਗ ਵੀਜ਼ੇ 'ਤੇ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਆ ਸਕਦੇ ਹੋ।

body: Home Affairs ਮੁਤਾਬਕ, 12 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਜਮ੍ਹਾਂ ਕੀਤੀਆਂ ਯੋਗ ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ ਦਾ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਹੀ ਨਿਯਮਾਂ ਤਹਿਤ ਹੋਵੇਗਾ ਜੋ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਲਾਗੂ ਸਨ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ 11 ਮਾਰਚ 2026 ਤੋਂ ਲਾਗੂ ਹੋਈਆਂ ਤਬਦੀਲੀਆਂ ਵੀ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਹਨ। ਮਾਰਚ ਤੋਂ ਬਿਨੈਕਾਰਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਅਪਲਾਈ ਕਰਨ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਆਪਣੇ ਸਪਾਂਸਰ ਅਤੇ ਆਪਣੀ ਟ੍ਰੇਨਿੰਗ ਨੌਮੀਨੇਸ਼ਨ, ਦੋਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਦੀ ਉਡੀਕ ਕਰਨੀ ਪੈਂਦੀ ਹੈ, ਸਿਵਾਏ ਉਦੋਂ ਜਦੋਂ ਸਪਾਂਸਰ ਕੋਈ ਕਾਮਨਵੈਲਥ ਏਜੰਸੀ ਹੋਵੇ।

ul: ਦੇਖੋ ਕਿ ਤੁਹਾਡਾ ਮੌਜੂਦਾ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਕਦੋਂ ਖ਼ਤਮ ਹੋ ਰਿਹਾ ਹੈ, ਅਤੇ ਉਸ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਛੱਡ ਦਿਓ।
ਅਪਲਾਈ ਕਰਨ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਪੱਕਾ ਕਰ ਲਓ ਕਿ ਸਪਾਂਸਰਸ਼ਿਪ ਅਤੇ ਨੌਮੀਨੇਸ਼ਨ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰ ਹੋ ਚੁੱਕੇ ਹਨ।
ਪਤਾ ਕਰੋ ਕਿ ਕੀ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਜਾਣ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਕੋਈ ਲੋੜੀਂਦੀ ਮੈਡੀਕਲ ਜਾਂਚ ਕਰਵਾ ਸਕਦੇ ਹੋ।
ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਮਿਲਣ ਦੀ ਅੰਦਾਜ਼ਨ ਤਾਰੀਖ਼ ਦੇ ਭਰੋਸੇ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਵਾਪਸੀ ਦੀ ਟਿਕਟ ਬੁੱਕ ਨਾ ਕਰੋ।

body: ਵਿਭਾਗ ਨੇ ਇਸ ਤਬਦੀਲੀ ਦਾ ਕੋਈ ਕਾਰਨ ਜਾਰੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੀਤਾ।

body.note: ਇਹ Department of Home Affairs ਦੀ ਆਮ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਹੈ, ਮਾਈਗ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਨ ਸਲਾਹ ਨਹੀਂ। ਆਪਣੀ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਬਾਰੇ ਸਲਾਹ ਲਈ ਕਿਸੇ ਰਜਿਸਟਰਡ ਮਾਈਗ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਨ ਏਜੰਟ ਜਾਂ ਵਕੀਲ ਨਾਲ ਗੱਲ ਕਰੋ।

body: One Nation has disendorsed Franco Guardiani, its candidate for the Labor-held seat of Preston in Melbourne's north, after social media posts circulated on Tuesday in which he described Adolf Hitler as the "GOAT", shorthand for "greatest of all time".

Victorian One Nation leader Warren Pickering said the party was appalled "at a time when Jewish Australians are experiencing unprecedented persecution", and that people holding such views "do not have a place in One Nation", the ABC reported. The party conceded its vetting process needed improvement.
Mr Guardiani confirmed to the ABC that the accounts were his. "The party does what it sees fit," he said, adding that he believed in free speech.

Nominations for the 28 November election closed on Monday, so Mr Guardiani will remain on the Preston ballot paper under the One Nation name, the ABC reported. One Nation volunteers are not expected to hand out how-to-vote cards at Preston polling places.
Preston is held by Labor on a margin of 2.1 per cent.
The disendorsement came on the same day Opposition Leader Jess Wilson confirmed the Coalition would put Labor, the Greens and the Socialists below One Nation on its how-to-vote cards.

body.note: A full list of candidates for every district is on the VEC website. If you see hateful content aimed at a community, Victoria's anti-vilification laws explain how to report it.

body: A former CFMEU organiser has told Victoria's Big Build royal commission that underworld figure Mick Gatto gave him an expensive gold bracelet, and that Mr Gatto sometimes intervened with the union on behalf of employers.
Paul Tzimas, who worked full-time as a union organiser, gave evidence on Wednesday, the third day of public hearings. AAP and NCA NewsWire both reported his evidence.

Mr Tzimas said he first refused the gift, then accepted it after Mr Gatto called it an "olive branch" and said he wanted nothing in return. He said he never wore it. "He never called upon any favours," Mr Tzimas told the commission, according to NCA NewsWire.
Asked by counsel assisting Chris Carr SC whether Mr Gatto would intervene with the union for employers, Mr Tzimas agreed.

Mr Carr put a list of names to the witness. Mr Tzimas identified 11 CFMEU organisers and health and safety representatives who, AAP reported, were affiliated with outlaw motorcycle gangs at the time or previously, and agreed the union had placed them on building sites.
He also agreed the union pushed hard to get its way, which he said was "to deliver outcomes for working people". He admitted breaking the law several times as an organiser and said he had been fined.

The first fortnight of hearings is focused on a two-day stoppage at the Gap Road level crossing removal in Sunbury in June 2022, when union delegates occupied the site and work resumed only after their demands were agreed.

WorkSafe inspector Quinton Drury told the commission the stoppage was given the lowest priority because priority is set by safety risk, not by disruption to projects. Inspectors arrived on 8 June 2022, after the dispute was resolved, and found only "minor" issues with piling holes, which were fixed during the inspection, AAP reported.

The royal commission is examining the integrity of the state's Big Build infrastructure program. Its hearings are running through the campaign for the 28 November state election, and its final report is due in August 2027. body: Cricket Australia (CA) will not open a new investigation into the 2018 Cape Town ball-tampering scandal, its chief executive Todd Greenberg said on Tuesday, after former Test opener Usman Khawaja wrote that the whole team knew about it.
Speaking on radio station SEN, Greenberg said there were "specific details in his book that contradict the versions that have been provided by others", according to ABC News and Reuters.

"We don't see any compelling reason to open the investigation or revisit this again," he said. He added that CA was comfortable with the outcome of the original investigation, which found that only captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and batter Cameron Bancroft knew of the plan.

In his autobiography, Sabr, Khawaja writes that discussion of tampering with the ball was not limited to a few players, and that sandpaper had been used before the Cape Town Test. He was not interviewed in the 2018 inquiry, the ABC reported. He also wrote that ball-tampering was common in the Sheffield Shield and named Victoria as the state best at it.
Responding to critics on social media on Tuesday, Khawaja said he had no commercial motive for the book, Reuters reported.

ul: Warner, one of the three players banned in 2018, said on Instagram on Monday that Khawaja's account was "100 per cent accurate" and described the original investigation as rushed and botched.
Bancroft declined to comment on Monday, Reuters reported. Former CA chief executive James Sutherland also declined to comment.
Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon denied knowledge of the plan in a joint statement in 2021.

body: Smith, Warner and Bancroft were banned or penalised by CA days after the incident in Cape Town in March 2018.

body: David Jones will close 19 of its 38 stores, including three in Melbourne, after receivers took control of the 188-year-old department store chain.

Receivers FTI Consulting announced the closures on Wednesday. "The receivers have made the difficult decision to proceed with an urgent restructure of the business," they said, according to AAP. FTI said the steps were "unavoidable if David Jones is to continue as a viable business", The Nightly reported.
The Victorian stores closing are Glen Waverley, Highpoint (in Maribyrnong) and Malvern Central, according to SmartCompany and The Nightly.

The other closures are seven stores in New South Wales, three in Western Australia (including the Hay Street Mall store in central Perth), two each in Queensland and South Australia, one in the ACT and the chain's only New Zealand store, in Auckland.

The stores will keep trading for now and no final closure date has been set. "We anticipate they will cease trading by the end of the year," FTI said, according to The Nightly. Staff at affected stores are being consulted, and flagship stores in capital-city CBDs have largely been spared.
David Jones employs about 6,000 people. The receivers have not said how many jobs will go.

FTI was appointed receiver last week by lender Hilco Capital, after McGrathNicol was appointed voluntary administrator, SmartCompany reported. The business had reportedly not paid rent to Westfield owner Scentre Group since September. Expressions of interest from potential buyers are due by the end of this week.
Charles Lloyd Jones, a member of the founding family who left the business in 1993, told AAP: "If you don't have a unique offer, then it's a race to the bottom with price."

en.dek: Receivers say an urgent restructure is needed. Most closing stores are in the suburbs; city flagships largely survive.

body: Eleven Australian soldiers killed in the First World War, and commemorated for more than a century as unknown, have been formally identified, the federal government announced for Remembrance Day.

Five of the men were from Victoria: Sergeant Charles Henry Nicholls of Ballarat, Lieutenant Howard Victor Morey of Lilydale, Second Lieutenant James Albert McMichael of Melbourne, Corporal Harry Maitland Whiteoak of Preston and Lance Corporal Alexander Joseph Jack of Brunswick, according to the list reported by ABC News and NCA NewsWire.

The identifications drew on historical research, archaeological work and DNA analysis. The Army's Unrecovered War Casualties team, the Office of Australian War Graves and the Commonwealth War Graves Commission did the work, with help from French authorities, independent researchers and the soldiers' descendants.

Four of the men served with the 2nd Australian Field Ambulance, the unit that included Corporal Whiteoak and Lance Corporal Jack. NCA NewsWire reported that all four were killed on 5 May 1917, during the Second Battle of Bullecourt in France, when an artillery shell hit a regimental aid post set up in a railway cutting. The Army team recovered them during an excavation at Riencourt-lès-Cagnicourt in April 2025.

body: Lieutenant Anderson was killed near Ypres in Belgium on 20 September 1917, aged 23. ABC News reported that his comrades buried him by the roadside under a wooden cross, and that an unknown soldier recovered from almost the same spot in 1919, whose grave record noted "Anderson on shirt", was reburied at Hooge Crater Cemetery. His headstone there can now carry his name.

Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Richard Marles, whose great-uncle was Lieutenant Anderson, said the identification was "deeply personal" for his family, ABC News reported. Veterans' Affairs Minister Matt Keogh said the work would "provide long-awaited answers for families" after generations of uncertainty.
